draft.title: Connotation and denotation
card: a word's dictionary meaning, the plain meaning that most people agree on.
the feeling or association a word carries beyond its dictionary meaning. It can be positive, negative or neutral.
Two words can share a denotation but have different connotations. Slim and skinny both describe a thin body, but slim feels positive and skinny can feel negative.
Writers choose words for their connotations to shape how a reader feels about a person, place or idea.
draft.remember: Denotation is what a word means. Connotation is how it feels.

a.q: Which pair of words has a similar denotation but different connotations?
a.why: Frugal and stingy both mean careful with money, but frugal feels positive and stingy feels negative. Happy and sad have opposite meanings. Table and chair are different objects, and run and runner are different word forms.
a.clue: Look for two words that mean about the same.

b.q: A review calls a new café cosy. A second review calls it cramped. What does this show?
opts: The first review is fact and the second a mistake
Both words carry the same connotation of comfort
b.why: Both words describe a small space, so their denotations are close. Cosy feels warm and positive, while cramped feels uncomfortable and negative. The difference is in the feeling each word carries, not in the dictionary meaning.
b.clue: Both describe a small space. How does each one feel?
